findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Name the exact GitLab CI schema source (canonical URL + expected `$schema` draft) and confirm `jsonschema>=4.18` can validate a YAML-parsed `.gitlab-ci.yml` against it offline (a one-line spike), so the 'no new dependency, no network' claim is verified rather than asserted.
evidence: Plan quote: 'the SCHEMA DOCUMENT ... is VENDORED into the repo at a pinned version with its source URL and retrieval date recorded, so the check needs no network and no new dependency'
Verified: `jsonschema` and `jsonschema.validate` EXIST; `jsonschema>=4.18` declared at pyproject.toml:64 — so the VALIDATOR is confirmed

UNVERIFIED (Partially-verified class): the plan names no canonical source URL for the schema, states no draft dialect (GitLab's CI schema is draft-07 with heavy conditional/patternProperties use), and does not confirm the YAML->dict->validate path or that `jsonschema>=4.18` supports the schema's declared `$schema`
ABSENCE: `search_files gitlab` and `Jenkinsfile` return no matches — this is a NET-NEW integration, so T3 applies rather than being an already-used internal path
findings.finding: The plan asserts GitLab's 'official JSON schema' can be vendored and validated OFFLINE via the already-declared `jsonschema` dependency, but does not verify the schema's canonical source/existence, its JSON-Schema draft dialect, or that `jsonschema>=4.18` supports that dialect against a YAML-parsed `.gitlab-ci.yml` — an unverified external-artifact + validator-compatibility assertion the portability AC depends on.
findings.location: Portability AC: '.gitlab-ci.yml validates against GitLab's official JSON schema, offline'
scenarios: The vendored schema declares a draft (e.g. draft 2020-12 or an unsupported meta-schema) that `jsonschema>=4.18` cannot resolve offline, so the check errors at import/validate time instead of validating the config
GitLab's published schema is only reachable via SchemaStore/a redirect the plan hasn't pinned, so 'source URL recorded' cannot be satisfied with a stable artifact

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a 2db2 AC that CI installs a pinned shellcheck and the extraction test emits a named, actionable failure (never a skip) when the binary is absent
evidence: Parent AC: 'The shellcheck prerequisite is PROVISIONED, not assumed: CI installs a pinned version, and the test FAILS with a named, actionable error when the binary is missing — it must never silently skip, which would void the "verifiable in-session" guarantee this AC block claims'

2db2 AC (nearest): 'shellcheck runs over script bodies extracted from all three configs and FAILS on an unparseable config (GitLab's own extractor returns true there; ours must not)' — covers unparseable-config detection only, not provisioning or missing-binary behaviour
No other sibling's roster ACs mention shellcheck at all
findings.finding: Parent portability AC requiring the shellcheck prerequisite to be PROVISIONED (CI installs a pinned version) and to FAIL with a named, actionable error when the binary is missing — never silently skip — is not delivered by any sibling. 2db2 (the sole portability child) covers only that 'shellcheck runs over script bodies extracted from all three configs and FAILS on an unparseable config'; it says nothing about installing a pinned shellcheck, nor about failing loudly (rather than skipping) when the binary is absent.
scenarios: CI image lacks shellcheck; the extraction test silently skips and reports green, voiding the 'verifiable in-session' guarantee the parent's AC block explicitly claims
A future runner drops the shellcheck install and the check quietly stops running with no error
findings.suggested_fix: Add an explicit 2db2 acceptance criterion mirroring the parent's provisioning AC: pin shellcheck in the test harness install, and assert the test hard-fails with a named error when shellcheck is not on PATH.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Extend 2db2's gitlab-schema AC to require the schema document be committed at a pinned version with its source URL and retrieval date recorded
evidence: Parent AC: '...the SCHEMA DOCUMENT is not [a declared dependency] — it is VENDORED into the repo at a pinned version with its source URL and retrieval date recorded, so the check needs no network and no new dependency'

2db2 AC: '.gitlab-ci.yml validates against GitLab's official JSON schema offline, using dependencies rebar already has' — asserts offline and no-new-dep, but not that the schema doc is committed/pinned with recorded provenance
No sibling covers the vendored-schema-with-provenance remainder
findings.finding: Parent portability AC requires the GitLab JSON SCHEMA DOCUMENT (distinct from the jsonschema validator) to be VENDORED into the repo at a pinned version with its source URL and retrieval date recorded, so the check needs no network and no new dependency. 2db2's covering AC narrows this to only 'validates against GitLab's official JSON schema offline, using dependencies rebar already has' — it delivers the offline + no-new-dependency outcome but omits the vendoring / pinned-version / source-URL / retrieval-date provenance requirement that the parent states as a first-class sub-clause.
scenarios: Implementer satisfies 'offline, using existing deps' by fetching the schema at build time from a cache or vendoring it without recording version/URL/date, so future drift or re-fetch is untraceable
findings.suggested_fix: Amend 2db2's schema-validation AC to state the schema document is vendored at a pinned version with source URL + retrieval date recorded in-repo.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile 2db2's 'no logic beyond credentials/timeout/exit-code mapping' clause with the strict flag, REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=always pin, bot-identity passthrough (1c1b) and workflow_dispatch mode-input mapping (4a44) the same workflow must carry
evidence: 2db2 AC: 'One runner-agnostic entrypoint; the three configs invoke it and carry no logic beyond credentials, timeout and exit-code mapping'

1c1b AC: 'reconcile-bridge.yml invokes the entrypoint in STRICT mode ... the per-provider smoke test asserts the strict flag is actually passed' and 'The reconciler workflow pins REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=always at the strict call site' and 'The workflow still sources the identity from BRIDGE_BOT_NAME/BRIDGE_BOT_EMAIL'

4a44 AC: 'its workflow_dispatch mode input is renamed to the new vocabulary ... The full mode -> new-surface mapping above is what the workflow implements' (mapping MODE values to preview / sync --max-changes N)
2db2 depends_on 1c1b and (via dependency chain) coexists with 4a44's edits to the same file
findings.finding: Conflicting assumption between 2db2 and siblings 1c1b/4a44 about how much logic the reconciler workflow config may carry. 2db2 asserts 'the three configs invoke [one entrypoint] and carry no logic beyond credentials, timeout and exit-code mapping', but 1c1b requires reconcile-bridge.yml to additionally pass a STRICT flag, pin REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=always at the strict call site, and source BRIDGE_BOT_NAME/BRIDGE_BOT_EMAIL into the entrypoint; and 4a44 requires the same workflow to carry a renamed workflow_dispatch mode input mapped to bridge preview / bridge sync --max-changes N. Those are invocation/mode-mapping logic beyond '{credentials, timeout, exit-code mapping}'.
scenarios: Implementer of 2db2 strips the workflow to bare credentials/timeout/exit-code and drops the strict flag, REBAR_SYNC_PUSH pin, or the workflow_dispatch mode-input mapping that 1c1b and 4a44 require, silently reverting 4c4f's disposition flip or removing the rollback brake
Reviewer of 4a44/1c1b re-adds mode-mapping/strict logic that 2db2's contract test flags as prohibited config logic
findings.suggested_fix: Broaden 2db2's clause to '...carry no logic beyond credentials, timeout, exit-code mapping, and the entrypoint invocation parameters owned by 1c1b/4a44 (strict flag, sync-push pin, author identity, mode-input mapping)', so the contract test whitelists those explicitly.

findings.finding: The portability AC mandates shellcheck over extracted script bodies, but the repo already made a deliberate, documented prior-art decision NOT to depend on shellcheck (bespoke dependency-free lint instead), and shellcheck is a heavy external binary, not a dependency rebar has — the plan reconciles neither.
findings.location: Portability AC line: 'shellcheck runs over script bodies extracted from all three configs, failing loudly on an unparseable config'
findings.suggested_fix: Cite det_lint.py's prior-art note in the AC and choose explicitly: (a) declare shellcheck a documented tool prerequisite provisioned by the test harness, or (b) route the extracted script bodies through the repo's existing dependency-free verify-command lint, noting why shellcheck's shell-specific checks are/aren't needed here.

findings.finding: The Portability AC requires shellcheck to run over extracted script bodies as an in-session verification gate, but the plan states no mechanism to obtain/pin the shellcheck binary. shellcheck is a standalone external tool (not a Python dependency), and the repo currently provisions no shellcheck (no Makefile target, no pre-commit hook) — unlike actionlint, which the repo installs via a pinned, SHA-256-verified Makefile target. Without a stated provisioning path this AC may silently no-op on a host lacking shellcheck, exactly the failure mode the plan is trying to eliminate for gh.
findings.location: Portability AC — 'shellcheck runs over script bodies extracted from all three configs, failing loudly on an unparseable config'
findings.suggested_fix: Add a repo-local shellcheck provisioning step modeled on the existing `actionlint-bin` Makefile target (pinned version + SHA-256 verification), and specify that the extraction/lint gate exits non-zero if shellcheck cannot be resolved.
